key_insight: Whole-brain modeling inferred higher cortical excitability in ALS, especially in motor-frontal regions, as a candidate mechanism for altered brain-wide activity propagation.
clinical_relevance: The framework offers individual-level research descriptors of ALS-related brain dynamics, but their clinical relevance remains unvalidated.
method: Characterized neuronal avalanche transitions in source-reconstructed resting-state magnetoencephalography.
Used tractography-informed reduced Wong–Wang models to simulate whole-brain dynamics.
Applied simulation-based inference to estimate recurrent excitation and global coupling.
evidence_signal: ALS patients showed significant avalanche-transition alterations versus healthy controls and higher model-inferred recurrent excitation; simulated excitation increases produced directionally consistent changes.
watch_item: Excitability estimates are model-dependent rather than direct measurements, and the abstract does not report sample size or independent clinical validation.
paper_title: Towards the Virtual Amyotrophic Lateral Sclerosis Patient: Inferring Cortical Excitability through Whole-Brain Dynamical Modeling
